messages:
Kate: :rotating_light: incident-bot fired for thread 1787770001 - we're seeing a surge of 429s from Stripe on webhook delivery and some API calls. Error body mentions "quota_exceeded". Customers hitting delayed provisioning.

incident-bot: Paging on-call (Kate) — Severity: P1 — Alert routed to #incidents and on-call PD.

Kate: I'm taking point. Can someone pull Stripe status and our webhook queue length? Also tag our Stripe AM.

stripe-status-bot: https://status.stripe.com — reported throttling affecting webhook delivery in multiple zones. (bot update: 45s ago)

Miguel: Observed endpoints: POST /v1/events returning 429 with header Retry-After: 60. Rate limit scope: account. Simultaneous auth 429s for service-account keys used by ingestion. Queue depth for webhook-processor up ~2200.

Priya: Customer impact: onboarding flows that require instant invoice confirmation are blocked. Preliminary count: ~95 customers impacted in last 15m, 25 marked critical (customer-facing purchases). Raising customer comms.

Kate: Mitigation idea A: flip to polling fallback for critical accounts and reduce aggressive retries to prevent amplification. Mitigation idea B: rotate to backup Stripe key for ingestion workers. Which is faster?

Dave: Polling toggle is easiest. Feature flag: ff.webhook.polling.force. I can flip now. Rotating keys needs verification with secrets manager and a short deploy.

Dave: Executing toggle: POST to internal FF service — confirmed set ff.webhook.polling.force = true. Deploy logs show change applied within 12s.

Miguel: Pushed retry config change to webhook workers: switched from fixed immediate retries to jittered exponential (min=4s, max=240s). Command used: 
```bash
kubectl set env deployment/webhook-worker RETRY_MIN=4 RETRY_MAX=240 RETRY_JITTER=true
kubectl rollout restart deployment/webhook-worker
```
Rollout initiated.

Priya: Posted a short customer-facing status message on status.redwood.ai: "We're experiencing delayed webhook delivery from a third-party payment provider; mitigation in progress. Expect intermittent delays for up to 2 hours."

Kate: Good. Also reduce non-critical outbound webhook retries (analytics, metrics sinks) to stay under Stripe limits. Miguel, can you add a circuit-breaker so we stop retrying when queue depth > 1500?

Miguel: Circuit-breaker added. Will drop retries and mark events for manual reprocess if queue > 1500. Monitoring queue metric now.

stripe-status-bot: Stripe update: investigating, potential config issue on their rate-limiter.

Dave: Quick note — I started switching 2 ingestion pods to alternate API key (stripe-key-backup). Throughput for those pods improved locally. Risk: backup key has lower rate limit but different quota window. Doing gradual roll.

Kate: Keep it gradual. We don't want to exhaust backup. Also log which customers get that key in case of reconciliation.

--- 20 minutes later ---

incident-bot: automated check at 1787771200 — webhook 429 rate down from 42% -> 15%. Queue trending down.

Priya: Update on customers: 40 resolved by polling fallback, 55 still queued, 0 payments lost. Sending targeted DMs to top-10 impacted customers.

Miguel: Metrics show retry fanout peaked at T0+3m because initial retry policy retried immediately. Traces attached to incident doc show high concurrency from retry logic.

stripe-status-bot: Stripe: increased request throughput for our account and removed a misapplied quota; monitoring the backlog.

Kate: OK. Start a controlled worker ramp: scale webhook-worker from 3 -> 7 over 15 minutes while watching 429% and queue. If 429 > 10% revert scale.

Dave: Scaling initiated: kubectl scale deployment/webhook-worker --replicas=7. Scaling window started.

Miguel: Observing 429s drop to single digits as scale and retries take effect. Queue processing rate improved. No new 503s.

Kate: Prepare to hand off in 1 hour. I'll document decision timeline, what we toggled, and key follow-ups: (1) postmortem to cover root cause (Stripe quota + our retry fanout), (2) ensure backup keys are tested in DR, (3) update alert thresholds for third-party 429s, (4) add proactive circuit-breaker rule for webhook ingestion.

Priya: Creating a SEV-1 incident doc (SEV-1-1787770001) and compiling logs, alerts, and customer tickets. RCA meeting scheduled tomorrow 09:30 PT.

Dave: Posting handoff note to PD. I'll continue monitoring and will escalate if any regression. Taking on-call at 1787773600. :white_check_mark:

stripe-status-bot: Stripe reports incident resolved on their side; recommend keeping slower retry and monitoring for 1 hour.

incident-bot: Incident mitigation logged by Kate at 1787771400. Please file bugs for improvements and follow-up actions.

Kate: Closing active mitigation tasks: keep polling fallback active for 2 hours, retain exponential backoff config, keep circuit-breaker threshold for 24h. Thanks team. :pray:

Miguel: I'll upload sampled traces and backlog processing logs to the incident doc.

Priya: Customer comms updated, targeted outreach to affected customers done. No escalations to legal/finance.

Dave: Handoff complete. Monitoring continued.
